edges.description: KCC3 deficiency reduces compound action-potential measures and nerve-conduction velocity in knockout mouse nerves.
Human pathology attributes the degenerative deficit to axonopathy caused ultimately by the KCC3 defect, with unknown intervening molecular steps.
intermediate_mechanisms: Molecular steps connecting KCC3 transport loss to axonal degeneration remain unresolved.

edges.description: Neuron-specific KCC3 loss produces abnormal motoneuron activity and early NMJ abnormalities in mice.
KCC3 deficiency is associated with abnormal commissural and corticospinal development, but the intervening developmental mechanism is unknown.
intermediate_mechanisms: Developmental steps connecting KCC3 loss to tract dysgenesis remain unresolved.

edges.description: Impaired impulse propagation is a mouse and ex vivo functional readout relevant to neuropathy, but a causal link to the human degenerative phenotype is not established.
The central and peripheral axonopathy manifests clinically as a progressive sensorimotor neuropathy.
Severe progressive sensorimotor neuropathy produces hypotonia.
Severe progressive sensorimotor neuropathy produces loss of reflexes.
Progressive sensorimotor neuropathy downstream of axonopathy contributes to amyotrophy.
Early NMJ abnormalities, denervation, and muscle atrophy co-occur downstream of neuron-specific KCC3 loss in mice; their direct causal ordering is unresolved.
Abnormal motoneuron activity is proposed to contribute to the human neuropathy, but this link remains model-derived.
Absence or hypoplasia of the major telencephalic commissures includes the corpus-callosum dysgenesis phenotype.
